name: City Council Budget Workshop
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council Budget Workshop

  February 2, 2017

A Budget Workshop of the City Council of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to
order by Mayor Bucknum at 9:35 a.m., on February 2, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo,
California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 26, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Mark Martinez, M.V.: asked that lights be installed at La Paws Dog Park if there are funds
available.

BUDGET WORKSHOP

1.  Welcome

  Facilitator Sherry Lund discussed the layout of the agenda and goals for the day.

City Council Minutes  1  February 2, 2017
   Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas summarized the budget process as well
  as the development of revenue projections and the Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) budget.
  She also outlined several topics that fall outside of today’s agenda including the history of
  the City’s authorized positions and a schedule for repayment of the Site C loan from the
  Mission Viejo Housing Authority.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs asked that staff develop a plan to pay off the loan as quickly as
  possible to be good stewards of the City’s money.

2.  Proposed Budget Calendar

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the proposed 2017-19 budget
  calendar.

3.  Mission, Vision and Organization Values

  Facilitator Lund outlined the City’s mission, vision and values statement.

4.  2015-17 Priorities

  Director Dyas discussed the strategic goals that were established by the City Council during
  the budget workshop two years ago. She also provided an overview of the accomplishments
  in relation to each strategic goal.

5.  Other Accomplishments

  Director Dyas outlined additional accomplishments that were presented in the agenda
  materials. These were outside of the six Council priorities and are reported to demonstrate
  the workload achieved by City staff.

6.  Ongoing Projects

  Director Dyas drew the Council Member’s attention to the list of ongoing projects across
  departments.

7.  Discretionary Reserves

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council member Goodell, to direct
  staff to develop a reserve policy based on the risk factor analysis provided by staff.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  2  February 2, 2017
 RECESS

At the hour of 11:09 a.m., Mayor Bucknum declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
11:23 a.m. with all five City Council Members present.

8.  Unfunded Liabilities

  Director Dyas provided an Unfunded Liabilities history. She noted that there are too many
  factors in flux right now and more information is needed before staff can make a
  recommendation to the City Council.

  By consensus, the City Council agreed that they will address the specific targets they wish
  to hit and a plan for reaching them again when more specific information from CalPERS
  becomes available.

9.  OCSD Contract

  Director Dyas provided a history of the Sheriff’s Department contract and stated that staff
  expects there will be an increase in the contract amount next year. She indicated that City
  Manager Wilberg and staff will be meeting with the Sheriff’s Department on February 22
  to discuss the Orange County Sheriff’s Department contract and anticipated costs.

RECESS FOR LUNCH

At the hour of 11:52 a.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting for lunch. The City Council
reconvened at 12:40 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

9.  OCSD Contract (continued)

  The City Council asked that the following questions be explored:

    Staffing costs vis-à-vis overtime. What are the cost savings of overtime? Is the
  staffing model as cost-effective as possible?

    What are the results of cost increases to the previous contracts?

    Has the addition of the Lake Forest Substation provided an improvement in
  response time?

    Has the field training center provided the anticipated uniformity in training, success
  rate with trainees, and success rate in minimizing liability in the field (both regular
  claims and Workers’ Compensation claims)?

    There are seven openings due to promotions to investigative services. Is the City
  paying for these?

City Council Minutes  3  February 2, 2017
     Prop 64 – recreational marijuana. What are the expected impacts and plans to
  address them, e.g., homeland security, impact on law enforcement (e.g., collisions,
  fatalities, and general enforcement) and legislation-related matters?

10.  Capital Improvement Program

  Director Dyas provided a summary of the 26 active Capital Improvement Projects.

  Community Services CIP Priorities

  The City Council provided a preliminary list of priorities as follows:

    Build the Felipe restroom. Council Members noted that this was promised to the
  public and is currently in the budget. The Felipe site is heavily used by youth and
  the restroom is badly needed.

    In order to assure that the Felipe restroom can be built, defer one park improvement.
  This matter will go to the Community Services Commission for a recommendation
  as to which one to defer.

    Keep the Library and Montanoso Recreation Center improvements recommended
  by staff on the priorities list.

    Review options and costs for Dog Park improvements. This item will be presented
  to the City Council for further discussion on February 14, 2017:
   Key card access
   Electricity
   Lighting

    Expand parking at Craycraft Park.

    Add trail connectivity.

    Community Services Commission to assess recreation items.

  Public Works CIP Priorities

    As a matter of information, staff will use Council’s approved 7-year plan to budget
  for public works CIP projects.

  Using the City Council’s preliminary priorities list provided at this meeting, staff will come
  back to the Council with specific cost information for each item. A final ranking will be
  made at that time, recognizing that there will likely not be enough money available to cover
  all of the items discussed.

City Council Minutes  4  February 2, 2017
 11.  Economic Development

  Director Dyas noted that staff provided the City Council with a complete copy of the Vision
  Plan document. The topic will be brought to the Council in March with recommendations
  for next steps including a budget of $791,000, which comes from the following sources:

    $351,000 remains in the 2016-17 budget.

    $160,000 is allocated for each of the two years of the 2017-19 budget.

    The Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) has awarded the
  City with a grant of $120,000 for the visioning process.

12.  Cultural Arts

  Director Dyas drew the Council’s attention to the draft Cultural Arts Master Plan which
  was included in the agenda materials.

  The City Council provided a list of recommendations as follows:

    Pursue the feasibility of a performance arts facility. This will be evaluated as part
  of the market feasibility study in the Cultural Arts Master Plan.

    Add $162,000 to the 2017-18 budget and $100,000 to the 2018-19 budget to be
  used for Cultural Arts Master Plan implementation funding.

    Cultural arts has a strong affinity to the Civic Center Core and Economic
  Development plans and should be considered in total.

13.  Regional Social Issues

  Director Dyas noted that staff placed material on this topic on the City Council dais prior
  to the meeting.

  Mrs. Dyas communicated that more staff time and resources will be needed to deal with
  community social issues such as sober living homes, legalization of marijuana, prescription
  drug addiction, and homelessness. These are complex sets of issues that cross many
  department boundaries and regional agency boundaries. There is no budgetary action to
  take at this point in time, but the Council should know that there may be emergent issues
  to address throughout the fiscal year.

City Council Minutes  5  February 2, 2017
 GENERAL DISCUSSION
 These
  The following matters were discussed and do not require action at the present time
  however, they may be taken up at a later date:

    OCTA is considering a sound wall along the 5 Freeway in Mission Viejo between
  Oso and Alicia Parkways.

    Council expressed opposition to connecting Avery to the Toll Road.

    Sober living homes: Holding landlords accountable for code violations, e.g., lack
  of heat and air conditioning in very crowded conditions.

    The City Attorney is finding an increased importance in legislative issues
  regarding State rights vs. Federal rights.

    Should the City consider adding language in the OCSD contract that establishes
  Mission Viejo’s priority if the State determines to become a "Sanctuary State,”
  e.g. that Mission Viejo will not participate in working against Federal Law? The
  City needs to be vigilant in following State sanctuary legislation.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 2:19 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, February 14, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 28, 2017

City Council Minutes  6  February 2, 2017
